humanities_role_explanation: MMMU-Pro is a general multi-discipline college-level multimodal benchmark across six disciplines (30 subjects). Humanities subjects (Art, Art Theory, Music, History, Literature) supply some items, but the competence tested is general multimodal understanding and robustness (text-only shortcuts, option count, vision-only input), not humanities scholarship.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Standard setting pairs image and text multiple-choice questions; the vision-only setting embeds question and options within a screenshot or photo, so only an image is fed to the model.
analytical_tasks_explanation: College-exam-style multiple-choice questions (up to 10 options) across disciplines, requiring subject knowledge and reasoning over diagrams, charts, photos, and tables. Humanities items (e.g., a political cartoon on U.S. expansionism, panning blur in photography, architectural systems from floor plans, musical key from notation, poem theme) are a minor share and are scored as single-letter answers. A secondary OCR extraction probe is measured by Levenshtein similarity.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Broad multi-discipline benchmark covering 30 subjects in six disciplines.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Qwen2-VL, InternVL2, LLaVA, VILA, Pixtral, MiniCPM-V, Idefics3, Phi-3.5-Vision.

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy, OCR accuracy via Levenshtein similarity.

summary: MMMU-Pro is a harder, more robust version of MMMU built by filtering text-only-answerable questions, augmenting options from 4 to 10, and adding a vision-only setting where questions are embedded in screenshots or photos. Model accuracy drops substantially relative to MMMU, and the paper analyzes the effects of CoT, OCR prompts, and error types.
key_findings: Performance falls 16.8 to 26.9 points relative to MMMU (Val). GPT-4o (0513) reaches 64.7 overall on MMMU-Pro. CoT generally helps but is weak or negative in Art and Design (LLaVA-OV-72B -17.12). OCR prompts have minimal effect. Reasoning errors rise to 46% of GPT-4o errors in the vision setting. Estimated human expert accuracy is 73.0 to 85.4.
evaluation_unit: multiple-choice question (1,730 questions each in standard and vision formats)
facets_explanation: Questions derive from MMMU, which the paper describes as drawn from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, so the answer keys come from existing assessment material. Options were augmented with GPT-4o, filtered by Claude 3.5, and reviewed twice by human experts. Answering requires college-level subject knowledge beyond the stimulus. Each item has one correct letter.
results_explanation: Table 1: GPT-4o (0513) 64.7 on MMMU-Pro overall, 54.0 (10 options), 49.7 (Vision), vs 69.1 on MMMU (Val). The largest gap is VILA-1.5-40B, 14.1 Vision vs 51.9 MMMU (Val), i.e. about 38 points, but the largest same-benchmark standard-to-vision comparison is VILA-1.5-40B 35.9 to 14.1 (22) or LLaVA-OV-72B 38.0 to 24.0 (14); the reported overall drop of 26.9 for VILA is taken as the upper bound, rounded to 27. Human expert estimates: Medium 80.8, High 85.4 overall; human gap computed as High 85.4 minus the 64.7 best model, about 21.
